math: Math — personal name: Math son of Mathonwy, lord of Gwynedd (Math uab Mathonwy oed arglwyd ar Wyned 'Math son of Mathonwy was lord over Gwynedd'); radical here (soft form Uath is separate)
mathonwy: Mathonwy — personal name, the father of Math (Math uab Mathonwy); genitive in a patronymic, no mutation
wyned: Gwyned (Gwynedd) — proper name, the kingdom of north-west Wales; soft-mutated (Gw>w) after ar 'over' (arglwyd ar Wyned 'lord over Gwynedd')
morgannhwc: Morgannwc (Morgannwg) — proper name, Morgannwg/Glamorgan, a region of south Wales (spelt here with -nhwc); radical, one of the cantrefs of the south listed after seith 'seven'
kyredigyawn: Keredigyawn (Ceredigion) — proper name, the region of west Wales, here spelt Kyredigyawn; radical (a phedwar Kyredigyawn 'and four of Ceredigion')
thri: tri (tri) — three (m.); numeral; spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and' (a thri Ystrat Tywi 'and three of Ystrat Tywi')
ymlyc: ymlyc (no secure modern form) — in the lap/bosom of, between; old preposition used before croth (ymlyc croth morwyn 'in the lap/womb of a maiden'); meaning approximate
croth: croth (croth) — womb, belly, lap; noun f.; radical, a genitive-like noun after ymlyc
kynwryf: kynwryf (cynnwrf) — commotion, tumult, uproar; noun m. (kynwryf ryuel 'a commotion of war'); radical, subject of the clause
ryuel: ryuel (rhyfel) — war; noun m.; radical (genitive after kynwryf)
llesteirei: llesteirio (llesteirio) — to hinder, obstruct, prevent; 3 sg. imperfect/conditional in -ei 'would hinder' (a'y llesteirei 'that would hinder him', with infixed y 'him'); ll unmutated, since the infixed y 'him' causes no soft mutation
goewin: Goewin — personal name: Goewin daughter of Pebin of Dol Pebin in Arfon, Math's foot-holder; radical
pebin: Pebin — personal name, the father of Goewin (Goewin uerch Pebin; Dol Pebin 'Pebin's meadow'); no mutation
dol: dol (dôl) — meadow, water-meadow, dale; noun f.; first element of place-names (Dol Pebin 'Pebin's meadow', Dol Penmaen); radical after o 'from' in a name
hoes: oes (oes) — age, lifetime, generation; noun f. (yn y hoes 'in her lifetime'); h-prefixed before the vowel after y 'her' (the possessive 'her' aspirates / adds h- to a vowel)
wydit: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; impersonal imperfect 'was known' (o'r a wydit yno 'of those that were known there'); soft-mutated (g lost) after the relative a
dathyl: Dathyl — second element of the place-name Kaer Dathyl, Math's court in Arfon (cf. Tathyl); radical
wastatrwyd: gwastatrwyd (gwastadrwydd) — constancy, steadiness, permanence; here (y wastatrwyd) his settled seat or constant abode (sense approximate); noun m.; soft-mutated (g lost) after y 'his'
gylchu: kylchu (cylchu) — to go round, make a circuit of, travel about; verbal noun, soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'to' and after the verb allei (ny allei gylchu y wlat 'he could not go round the land'; y gylchu y wlat 'to go round the land')
giluathwy: Giluathwy (Gilfaethwy) — personal name: Gilfaethwy son of Don, brother of Gwydion; radical
don: Don — personal name; in a patronymic (uab Don 'son of Don'): Gilfaethwy, Euyd and Gwydion are sons of Don, and Don is Math's sister (nyeint ueibon y chwaer)
euyd: Euyd (Eueid, Eufydd) — personal name: Euyd son of Don, brother of Gilfaethwy; this text names Euyd where one would expect Gwydion; radical (after a 'and' before a vowel)
nyeint: nei (nai) — nephew; plural nyeint 'nephews' (modern neiaint); (o nyeint ueibon y chwaer 'as/of nephews, sons of his sister'); the sense of o here is uncertain; radical
ueibon: mab (mab) — son; plural meibon 'sons' (modern meibion), spelt ueibon; soft-mutated (m>u) as a noun in apposition to the preceding nyeint ('nephews, sons of his sister')
giluaethwy: Giluaethwy (Gilfaethwy) — personal name, a variant spelling of Giluathwy: Gilfaethwy son of Don; radical
charu: caru (caru) — to love; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after y 'her' (a'y charu 'and (to) love her')
wnay: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. imperfect 'would do, was to do', spelt -ay for -ei (na wydat beth a wnay ymdanei 'that he did not know what he should do about her'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
ymdanei: am (am) — about, around, concerning; conjugated preposition 3 sg. f. 'about her' (modern amdani), with prefixed y- (ymdanei); no mutation
atueilaw: atueilaw (adfeilio, probable descendant) — to decay, fall away, waste; verbal noun (yn atueilaw 'wasting away', said of his colour and looks); meaning inferred from context; no mutation (vowel)
guydyon: Gwydion — personal name: Gwydion son of Don (also spelt Wydyon, Gwydyon), Math's nephew; Guydyon with u for w; radical (after the particle y in heb y Guydyon 'said Gwydion')
urawd: brawt (brawd) — brother; noun m., d spelling t; soft-mutated (b>u) after y 'his' (Guydyon y urawd 'Gwydion his brother', i.e. Gilfaethwy's brother)
synnyeit: synnyaw (synhwyro; modern synnu has a different sense) — to perceive, observe, notice; here synnyeit (dydgweith arnaw yn graf 'looking at him intently one day'), a 3 sg. past form whose exact ending is uncertain; radical
ham: am (am) — about, for; preposition, in pa ham 'why' (lit. 'what about/for'), spelt ham with h- after pa; the h is aspiration after pa
gwelaf: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. present 'I see' (Gwelaf arnat 'I see on you'); radical, verb in first place with no particle
frwytha: ffrwytho (ffrwytho) — to bear fruit, prosper, avail; 3 sg. present 'it avails, profits' (ny frwytha ymi 'it does not avail me'); ff does not mutate, single f is the scribe's spelling; after ny 'not'
adef: adef (addef) — to confess, admit, acknowledge; verbal noun (y adef y neb 'to confess it to anyone'); no mutation (vowel)
kynedyf: kynedyf (cynneddf) — inborn quality, special property, nature, endowment; noun f. (kynedyf Math 'Math's special property'); radical, object of wdost
hustyng: hustyng (hustyng) — whisper, secret word; noun m. (ba hustyng bynnac 'whatever whisper'); radical (h does not mutate)
kyuarfo: kyuarfot (cyfarfod) — to meet, come upon, reach; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may meet' (o ry kyuarfo y guynt ac ef 'if the wind should meet it'); the perfective ry would be expected to soften k>g, not shown in the spelling
guynt: gwynt (gwynt) — wind; noun m.; radical gu- (= gw-) after the article y
guybyd: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. present/future 'will know' (ef a'y guybyd 'he will know it', with infixed y 'it'); g kept after infixed y
caru: caru (caru) — to love; verbal noun, fronted for emphasis before yd wyt ti (caru Goewin yd wyt ti 'it is loving Goewin that you are'); radical
dromhaf: trwm (trwm) — heavy; superlative trymaf, spelt dromhaf 'heaviest', sigh being a feminine noun; soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine noun ucheneit (ucheneit dromhaf 'the heaviest sigh')
ucheneidaw: ucheneidaw (ochneidio) — to sigh, groan; verbal noun, with th 'your' before it (a'th ucheneidaw 'and your sighing'); no mutation (vowel)
goruydir: goruot (gorfod) — to overcome, prevail, succeed; impersonal present 'one prevails' (nyt o hynny y goruydir 'it is not by that that one prevails'); radical after the particle y
dygyuori: dygyuori (dygyfori) — to muster, rally, stir up; verbal noun, longer form of dygyuor (dygyuori Gwyned a Phowys a Deheubarth 'to muster Gwynedd and Powys and Deheubarth')
gwyned: Gwyned (Gwynedd) — proper name, the kingdom of north-west Wales; radical (object of dygyuori; Gwyned a Phowys a Deheubarth)
phowys: Powys — proper name, the kingdom of east and mid Wales; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
deheubarth: Deheubarth — proper name, the southern realm (deheu 'south' + parth 'part'); radical
lawen: llawen (llawen) — glad, merry; adjective, soft-mutated (ll>l) as the complement after byd (a byd lawen di 'and be glad')
paraf: peri (peri) — to cause, bring about, arrange; 1 sg. present 'I will cause' (a mi a'y paraf yt 'and I will bring it about for you'); p kept after infixed y 'it'
uath: Math — personal name; soft-mutated (M>u) after at 'to' (at Uath uab Mathonwy 'to Math son of Mathonwy') and in yguelei Uath (cause there uncertain)
bryuet: pryf (pryf) — creature, animal, worm; plural pryfet 'creatures' (modern pryfed), spelt bryuet; soft-mutated (p>b) after ryw 'kind of' (y ryw bryuet 'some kind of creatures')
henw: enw (enw) — name; noun m. (eu henw wy 'their name'); h- prefixed to the vowel after eu 'their'
hobeu: hob (hob) — pig, hog; plural hobeu, the name the strange beasts are first given before moch (Hobeu, Arglwyd 'Hobs, lord'); radical
aniueileit: aniueil (anifail) — animal, beast; noun m., plural aniueileit (modern anifeiliaid); radical (vowel)
bychein: bychan (bychan) — small, little; adjective, plural bychein (modern bychain) agreeing with the plural aniueileit (aniueileit bychein 'small animals'); radical after its noun
chic: kic (cig) — meat, flesh; noun m., spirant-mutated (c>ch) after no 'than' (guell eu kic no chic eidon 'their flesh is better than the flesh of oxen')
eidon: eidon (eidion) — ox, bullock, cattle (beef); noun m., plural/collective; radical (genitive after chic)
ynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present 'they are' (Bychein ynt wynteu 'small they are'); no mutation
symudaw: symudaw (symud) — to change, alter, move; verbal noun (yn symudaw enweu 'changing names'); radical
enweu: enw (enw) — name; plural enweu (modern enwau); object of the verbal noun symudaw, no mutation (vowel)
biewynt: piau (piau) — to own, be the property of; pwy biewynt wy 'whose are they?' (lit. 'who owns them'); the -ynt is a 3 pl. ending; soft-mutated (p>b) after the interrogative pwy; the exact analysis of the form is uncertain
anuonet: anuon (anfon) — to send; impersonal preterite 'was sent' (yd anuonet idaw o Annwn 'was sent to him from Annwn'); no mutation (vowel), after particle yd
cadw: cadw (cadw) — to keep, preserve, retain; verbal noun (yd ys yn cadw o'r enw hwnnw 'keeping of that name'); radical after yn
hwch: hwch (hwch) — sow; noun f.; radical (hanner hwch 'half a sow')
hob: hob (hob) — pig, hog; singular of hobeu (hanner hwch, hanner hob 'half sow, half hob'); noun m.; radical
keffir: caffael (cael) — to get, obtain; impersonal present 'is got' (ba furuf y keffir wy y gantaw ef 'by what means are they got from him'); c unmutated after the particle y
deudecuet: deudecuet (deuddegfed) — twelfth; ordinal (ar uyn deudecuet 'with me as the twelfth'); radical, the nasal mutation being written on uyn
beird: bardd (bardd) — poet, bard; plural beird 'poets' (yn rith beird 'in the guise of poets'); radical
necau: necau (no secure modern form) — to kill, destroy, strangle; verbal noun (ef a ry eill ych necau 'he may kill you'); meaning approximate
trawscwyd: trawscwyd (trawsgwydd) — a crossing, venture, hazard, mishap; noun m.; here nit drwc uyn trawscwyd i 'my venture is not bad'; sense approximate; radical after uyn 'my' (nasal mutation written on uyn)
kerda: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; 2 sg. imperative 'go!' (kerda ragot 'go on your way'); radical
deguyr: deg + gwyr (deg gwyr) — ten men; the numeral deg 'ten' and gwyr 'men' written as one word (a deguyr gyt ac wynt 'and ten men with them')
heredigyawn: Keredigyawn (Ceredigion) — proper name; nasal mutation (c>ngh) after yg 'in', spelt yg Heredigyawn with the h standing for the gh of the nasal (hyt yg Heredigyawn 'as far as in Ceredigion')
elwir: galw (galw) — to call, name; impersonal present 'is called' (y lle a elwir 'the place that is called'); g lost by soft mutation after the relative a
rudlan: Rudlan (Rhuddlan) — proper name, in Rudlan Teiui 'Rhuddlan Teifi', the place of Pryderi's court in Ceredigion (probably rud 'red' + glan 'bank'); no mutation
teiui: Teiui (Teifi) — proper name, the river Teifi; genitive in Rudlan Teiui, no mutation
awrhon: awrhon (yr awrhon, awr hon) — this hour, now; awr 'hour' + hon 'this' run together, adverbial (yr awrhon 'now, at the present'); no mutation
neillaw: neillaw (no modern form) — one side; neill 'other, one' + llaw 'hand' written as one word (ar neillaw Pryderi 'at Pryderi's side'); noun f.; no mutation shown
gossodet: gossot (gosod) — to place, set, seat; impersonal preterite 'was placed' (y gossodet Guydyon 'Gwydion was seated'); radical after y
cahel: caffael (cael) — to get, have; verbal noun, spelt cahel beside cael (da yw genhym ni cahel kyuarwydyt 'we are glad to get a tale'); radical
gwreinc: gwreng (gwreng) — common people, lower folk; collective noun, spelt gwreinc (rei o'r gwreinc racco 'some of the folk yonder'); sense here is approximately 'people'; radical
delher: dyuot (dod) — to come; impersonal present subjunctive 'one comes' (y nos gyntaf y delher at wr mawr 'the first night that one comes to a great man'); radical d after the particle y
penkerd: pencerdd (pencerdd) — chief of song, chief poet; noun m. (dywedut o'r penkerd 'to be told by the chief poet'); radical after the article r, o 'by' marks the agent
gyuarwydyd: kyuarwydyt (cyfarwyddyd) — tale, story; noun m., spelt with -yd; soft-mutated (k>g) as the object of dywedaf (Mi a dywedaf gyuarwydyd 'I will tell a tale')
wydyon: Gwydion — personal name (Gwydyon, Wydyon); soft-mutated (G>w) after gan 'with', after e 'to' and in apposition to ynteu (Ynteu Wydyon 'he, Gwydion')
didanu: didanu (diddanu) — to comfort, entertain, amuse; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaeth (didanu y llys a wnaeth 'he entertained the court'); radical
ymdidaneu: ymdidan (ymddiddan) — conversation, talk; plural ymdidaneu (modern ymddiddanion); noun m., radical after ar
chyuarwydyt: kyuarwydyt (cyfarwyddyd) — tale, storytelling; noun m., spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyuarwydyt 'and (with) a tale')
didan: didan (diddan) — pleasant, entertaining, comforting; adjective as predicate after yn (yn didan gan Pryderi ymdidan ac ef 'and pleasant to Pryderi was conversing with him'); d not shown softened after yn
tauawt: tauawt (tafod) — tongue; noun, treated here as f. since the next adjective is soft-mutated (Tauawt lawn da 'a full good tongue'); radical
lawn: llawn (llawn) — full, complete, perfect; adjective, soft-mutated (ll>l) after the feminine noun tauawt
teu: teu (tau) — your, thy; possessive adjective placed after its noun (y teu di 'yours, your own'), with the pronoun di echoing; no mutation
ymadolwyn: ymadolwyn (no modern form) — to entreat, petition, parley with; verbal noun, ym- + adolwyn 'beseech' (ymadolwyn a thidi 'to parley with you'); sense approximate; radical
elont: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. present subjunctive 'may go' (nat elont y genhyf 'that they may not go from me'); radical
hilyont: hilio (hilio) — to breed, multiply, bear young; 3 pl. present subjunctive 'may breed' (yny hilyont eu deu kymeint 'until they breed twice as many'); radical
geireu: gair (gair) — word; plural geireu (modern geiriau); radical after the article r with a plural
gallaf: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 sg. present 'I can' (Sef ual y gallaf 'this is how I can'); radical after the particle y
nacaha: nacau (nacáu) — to refuse, deny; 2 sg. imperative 'refuse!' (ac nacaha ui ohonunt 'and refuse me of them'); the sense needs a lost negative, na, as the established text notes; radical
dangossaf: dangos (dangos) — to show, offer; 1 sg. present/future 'I will show' (Auory minheu a dangossaf gyfnewit 'tomorrow I for my part will show an exchange'); the soft form after a is not shown in the spelling
lletty: llety (llety) — lodging, quarters; noun m. (y'r lletty 'to the lodging'); radical after the article
chawni: caffael (cael) — to get; 1 pl. future/present chawn 'we shall get' with the pronoun ni 'we' run on (ny chawni y moch 'we shall not get the pigs'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ny
drawscwyd: trawscwyd (trawsgwydd) — venture, hazard, means, mishap; noun m.; soft-mutated (t>d) after pa 'what' (pa drawscwyd 'by what means / what venture'); sense approximate
keir: caffael (cael) — to get; impersonal present 'is got' (pa drawscwyd y keir wynteu 'by what means are they to be got'); radical c after the particle y
geluydodeu: kelvydyd (celfyddyd) — art, skill, craft; noun f., plural kelvydodeu (modern celfyddydau); soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'his' (yn y geluydodeu 'into his arts')
dechreuawt: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 sg. preterite 'began' (ac y dechreuawt dangos y hut 'and he began to show the enchantment'); radical after y
hudwys: hudaw (hudo) — to enchant, conjure by magic; 3 sg. preterite 'conjured' in -wys (yd hudwys deudec emys 'he conjured twelve emys'); radical after yd
deudec: deudeg (deuddeg) — twelve; numeral, c spelling g, followed by a singular noun (deudec milgi, deudec torch); no mutation
emys: emys (no modern form) — a kind of horse or hunting beast, conjured among the dogs and horses; noun m.; meaning uncertain (perhaps steeds, since the same twelve are later meirch 'horses')
milgi: milgi (milgi) — greyhound; noun m., singular after a numeral (deudec milgi 'twelve greyhounds'); radical
bronwyn: bronwyn (bronwyn) — white-breasted; adjective, bron 'breast' + gwyn 'white' (milgi bronwyn du pob un 'greyhounds white-breasted, black each one'); follows its noun, no mutation
torch: torch (torch) — torque, neck-ring, collar; noun f. (deudec torch 'twelve collars'); radical after a numeral
kynllyuan: kynllyuan (cynllyfan) — leash, lead; noun m., singular after a numeral (deudec kynllyuan 'twelve leashes'); radical
kyfrwy: kyfrwy (cyfrwy) — saddle; noun m., singular after a numeral (deudec kyfrwy 'twelve saddles'); radical
frwyneu: ffrwyn (ffrwyn) — bridle; noun f., plural ffrwyneu (modern ffrwynau); the single f is the scribe's spelling of ff, no mutation (a'r frwyneu 'and the bridles'; eu frwyneu 'their bridles')
graessaw: graessaw (graesaw; later croeso) — welcome; noun m. (a graessaw wrthyt 'and welcome to you'); radical; modern croeso is the same word in a later form
rydit: rydit (rhyddid) — release, ransom, satisfaction; noun m. (llyma rydit yti am y geir 'here is a ransom for you for the word'); radical
rodut: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 2 sg. imperfect/conditional in -ut 'you would give' (nas rodut 'that you would not give them'); radical after nas
guerthut: gwerthu (gwerthu) — to sell; 2 sg. imperfect/conditional in -ut 'you would sell' (nas guerthut 'that you would not sell them'); the soft form expected after nas is not shown
deudeg: deudeg (deuddeg) — twelve; numeral, spelt with g (y deudeg meirch 'the twelve horses'); no mutation
gyueir: kyueir (cyfair) — even, complete, in order; adjective, meaning approximate (ual y maent yn gyueir 'just as they are, all together'); soft-mutated (k>g) after predicative yn
torcheu: torch (torch) — torque, collar; plural torcheu (modern torchau); radical after eu 'their' (eu torcheu 'their collars')
kynllyuaneu: kynllyuan (cynllyfan) — leash, lead; plural kynllyuaneu (modern cynllyfanau); radical after eu 'their'
rithassei: rithyaw (rhithio) — to shape, conjure into a form; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had shaped' in -assei (y rei hynny a rithassei ef o'r madalch 'those he had shaped out of the toadstools'); r unchanged (rh does not mutate)
madalch: madalch (madarch) — mushrooms, toadstools, fungi; collective plural noun; radical after the article r ('o'r madalch' 'out of the toadstools')
gaussant: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 3 pl. preterite 'they got, they had' in -ssant (Sef a gaussant yn y kynghor 'this is what they had in their counsel'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
kymeryssant: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 3 pl. preterite 'they took' in -yssant (y kymeryssant wy ganheat 'they took leave'); radical after y
ganheat: kanhead (caniatâd) — leave, permission; noun m., in kymryt ganheat 'to take leave'; soft-mutated (c>g) as object of the verb
geimeit: keimeit (cf. ceimiaid) — companions, fellows; plural address (A geimeit 'O fellows'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the vocative a; meaning approximate
bryssur: bryssur (brysur) — hasty, quick, busy; adjective, adverbial after yn (yn bryssur 'hastily'); b not shown softened after yn
phara: parhau (parhau) — to last, continue, endure; 3 sg. present/future 'will last' (Ny phara yr hut 'the enchantment will not last'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after ny
ygwarthaf: yg + gwarthaf (ar warthaf) — upon, at the top of; gwarthaf 'summit, top' (hyt ygwarthaf Keredigyawn 'to the upper part of Ceredigion'); written as one word, the g the trace of yn + gwarthaf; sense approximate
achaus: achaws (achos) — cause, reason; noun m., spelt achaus with u (o achaus hynny 'because of that'); radical
mochtref: Mochtref — place-name (moch 'pigs' + tref 'homestead'), the name of the places where the pigs spent the night; radical
elenit: Elenit (Elenydd) — proper name, the mountain upland of mid Wales (dros Elenit 'over Elenydd'); no mutation
keri: Keri (Ceri) — proper name, Ceri in mid Wales, between Ceri and Arwystli; radical
arwystli: Arwystli — proper name, a district of mid Wales; radical
powys: Powys — proper name, the kingdom of east and mid Wales; radical (nasal mutation not shown after ym 'in': ym Powys)
mochnant: Mochnant — place-name in Powys (moch 'pigs' + nant 'valley'), named from the pigs; radical
odynha: odyna (oddyna) — from there, then, afterwards; adverb, spelt odynha (variant with h) beside odyna; no mutation
ros: Ros (Rhos) — proper name, the cantref Rhos in north Wales (cantref Ros); radical
gwydyon: Gwydion — personal name: Gwydion son of Don (Gwydyon); radical (the y before it in heb y Gwydyon is the particle that introduces a named speaker)
gyrchwn: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to go to, make for; 1 pl. present/future 'we will make for' (ni a gyrchwn 'we will make for'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
kedernit: kedernit (cadernid) — strength, stronghold, fastness; noun m. (kedernit Gwynet 'the stronghold of Gwynedd'); radical
gwynet: Gwynet (Gwynedd) — proper name, the kingdom of north-west Wales, spelt with t; radical (genitive after kedernit)
lluydaw: lluydaw (lluyddu) — to muster, raise a host, march with an army; verbal noun (yd ys yn lluydaw yn an ol 'is mustering a host after us'); radical after yn
arllechwoed: Arllechwoed (Arllechwedd) — proper name, a district of Gwynedd, ar 'on' + llechwedd 'slope'; radical after o in o Arllechwoed
creu: creu (crau) — sty, pen, enclosure for animals; noun m. (gwneuthur creu y'r moch 'making a sty for the pigs'); radical
creuwryon: Creuwryon — place-name, the name given to the upper township after the sty (creu); the second element is of uncertain meaning; radical
tathyl: Tathyl — second element of Kaer Tathyl, Math's court, spelt Tathyl beside Dathyl; radical
hwyret: hwyret (hwyred) — slowness, lateness; abstract noun from hwyr 'late, slow' (Ryued uu hwyret y kerdyssawchi 'strange it was how slow you travelled'); radical
kerdyssawchi: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, travel; 2 pl. preterite 'you travelled' in -yssawch with chi 'you' run on (kerdyssawch chi); radical after y
aethawch: mynet (mynd) — to go; 2 pl. preterite 'you went' (yd aethawch yn eu hwysc 'that you went after them'); radical
hwysc: hwysc (cf. gwysg) — track, trail, wake; yn eu hwysc 'after them, on their track'; the h- after eu 'their' is unexplained, cf. modern yn ei wysg 'after him'; meaning approximate
issot: issot (isod) — below, lower down; adverb, (y cantref arall issot 'the other cantref below'); no mutation
clywynt: klywet (clywed) — to hear; 3 pl. imperfect 'they heard' (llyma y clywynt yr utkyrn 'behold, they heard the horns'); radical after y
